source: Hand-written by the Interim team (2026-10-10) for scripts/synthea/import_synthea.py. LOINC and SNOMED codes are the ones Synthea emits (checked against the committed run).
rationale: Every code list, window and parsing word list the importer uses lives here (CLAUDE.md §13: code reads tables, it does not hardcode clinical numbers). Nothing in this file is used by the runtime rules engine; it shapes synthetic fixtures only.
label: Synthea synthetic EHR (simulated)

nsclc.rationale: Same five codes as scripts/synthea/keep_nsclc.json (a test keeps them equal). Stage is read from the TNM-stage concept; the unstaged concept gives stage null.

windows.rationale: Notes and encounters 'in the last 12 months' means reference_date - 365 days < date <= reference_date. At most 6 notes per participant keeps the committed fixture small (size budget ~1.5 MB) while every emergency-encounter note is always included.

encounter_class.rationale: FHIR v3-ActCode encounter class -> the plain words used in the fixtures.

vitals.rationale: Baseline vitals from Synthea Observations (LOINC). Blood pressure comes from the components of the 85354-9 panel. Every value is simulated.

smoking.rationale: Tobacco smoking status (LOINC 72166-2) answer concepts -> status. Fallback when no observation exists: the note's '# Social History' sentence, matched by the regexes below (first match wins).

cancer_therapy.rationale: A MedicationAdministration is cancer therapy when its reason (reasonReference display) names a malignancy. Dental fluoride and eye-exam drops are administrations too and are excluded by this rule.

ingredient.rationale: Documented heuristic for the 'leading ingredient' of an RxNorm clinical-drug display (e.g. '24 HR metoprolol succinate 100 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet' -> 'metoprolol'). Steps: (1) remove a trailing [Brand]; (2) split combinations on ' / ' (each part is one ingredient; the first is the leading ingredient); (3) per part, drop a leading package/duration quantity ('24 HR', '1 ML', '120 ACTUAT', 'NDA020503'); (4) keep the words before the first word that starts with a digit (the strength); (5) cut at the first comma ('insulin isophane, human' -> 'insulin isophane'); (6) lowercase; (7) drop trailing salt and formulation words, unless the first word is itself a salt word ('sodium fluoride' and 'sodium chloride' stay whole). It is a string heuristic, not RxNorm ingredient lookup (no RxNorm API, no licence).
